questions.question: Q1 (MIT 8101): A commercial bank in Nigeria is implementing COBIT 2019 to bridge the gap between business risk and technical controls. Which domain of the Governance and Management objectives specifically focuses on the end-to-end delivery and support of IT services, including security management?
questions.explanation: In COBIT 2019, the DSS (Deliver, Service and Support) domain addresses operational delivery, service continuity, data management, and operational security controls.

questions.question: Q2 (MIT 8101): According to the Henderson-Venkatraman Strategic Alignment Model, when an enterprise aligns its IT Strategy directly with business strategy to drive organizational transformation, which alignment perspective is being executed?
questions.explanation: The Competitive Potential alignment perspective looks at how business strategy leverages IT strategy to create new competitive capabilities and market advantages.

questions.question: Q3 (MIT 8101): During an Audit under the Nigeria Data Protection Act (NDPA / NDPR), a company suffers a major breach exposing customer PII. What is the fundamental operational difference between Incident Management and Problem Management under ITIL v4 during this breach?

options.A: Incident Management fixes the root cause, while Problem Management handles user communication.
options.B: Incident Management focuses on restoring normal service operation as quickly as possible, while Problem Management analyzes the underlying root cause to prevent recurrence.
options.C: Incident Management handles compliance reporting, while Problem Management performs infrastructure maintenance.
options.D: Incident Management is a governance function, while Problem Management is purely executive.

questions.explanation: Incident Management prioritizes rapid service restoration (workarounds), whereas Problem Management aims to diagnose root causes and prevent incident recurrence.

questions.question: Q4 (MIT 8101): An enterprise IT department is evaluating a cloud deployment where the provider controls infrastructure, operating system, and middleware, but the organization manages application code and configuration. Which cloud deployment service model does this represent?
questions.explanation: PaaS provides the OS, runtime environment, middleware, and database engines, leaving application code execution and custom software settings to the client.

questions.question: Q5 (MIT 8101): When auditing General IT Controls (GITC) versus Application Controls in an ERP deployment (e.g., SAP or Oracle), which of the following is classified strictly as an Application Control?

options.A: Physical security access logs for the enterprise data center.
options.B: User Access Provisioning and Deprovisioning policy reviews.
options.C: Automated 3-way matching of Purchase Orders, Receiving Reports, and Supplier Invoices.
options.D: Data Center Backup and Disaster Recovery testing procedures.

questions.explanation: Automated 3-way matching is embedded within the business logic of the application software itself (Application Control), whereas physical security and user provisioning are General IT Controls.

questions.question: Q193 (MIT 8101): During an Audit under the Nigeria Data Protection Act (NDPA / NDPR), a company suffers a major breach exposing customer PII. What is the fundamental operational difference between Incident Management and Problem Management under ITIL v4 during this breach?

options.A: Incident Management fixes the root cause, while Problem Management handles user communication.
options.B: Incident Management focuses on restoring normal service operation as quickly as possible, while Problem Management analyzes the underlying root cause to prevent recurrence.
options.C: Incident Management handles compliance reporting, while Problem Management performs infrastructure maintenance.
options.D: Incident Management is a governance function, while Problem Management is purely executive.

questions.explanation: Incident Management prioritizes rapid service restoration (workarounds), whereas Problem Management aims to diagnose root causes and prevent incident recurrence.

questions.question: Q194 (MIT 8101): An enterprise IT department is evaluating a cloud deployment where the provider controls infrastructure, operating system, and middleware, but the organization manages application code and configuration. Which cloud deployment service model does this represent?
questions.explanation: PaaS provides the OS, runtime environment, middleware, and database engines, leaving application code execution and custom software settings to the client.

questions.question: Q195 (MIT 8101): When auditing General IT Controls (GITC) versus Application Controls in an ERP deployment (e.g., SAP or Oracle), which of the following is classified strictly as an Application Control?

options.A: Physical security access logs for the enterprise data center.
options.B: User Access Provisioning and Deprovisioning policy reviews.
options.C: Automated 3-way matching of Purchase Orders, Receiving Reports, and Supplier Invoices.
options.D: Data Center Backup and Disaster Recovery testing procedures.

questions.explanation: Automated 3-way matching is embedded within the business logic of the application software itself (Application Control), whereas physical security and user provisioning are General IT Controls.

questions.question: Q352 (MIT 8113): In a Scrum development team building a Fintech payment super-app, who holds sole accountability for prioritizing the Product Backlog to maximize business value?
questions.explanation: The Product Owner is explicitly accountable for managing and prioritizing items in the Product Backlog to optimize product value.

questions.question: Q353 (MIT 8113): A neo-bank shifts its core platform from a monolithic architecture to a microservices architecture running on Kubernetes containers. What is the primary operational trade-off of this architectural transition?

options.A: Lower system agility and restricted deployment frequency.
options.B: Increased organizational complexity, network latency considerations, and distributed tracing requirements.
options.C: Inability to scale independent services autonomously.
options.D: Complete loss of database transactional consistency across all microservices.

questions.explanation: Microservices enhance modular scalability and rapid deployment but introduce system complexity, distributed network dependencies, and complex monitoring/tracing requirements.

questions.question: Q354 (MIT 8113): Applying the ADKAR Model (Prosci) to an enterprise-wide AI implementation, an organization conducts extensive technical training workshops, but employees refuse to adopt the new tool due to job security fears. Which ADKAR element failed to be addressed first?
questions.explanation: Without fostering Awareness of the need for change and Desire to support it, technical training (Knowledge/Ability) fails to drive adoption.

questions.question: Q355 (MIT 8113): A digital ride-hailing or payment platform experiences increased value to existing users as more merchants and customers join the ecosystem. What type of competitive advantage/moat does this represent?
questions.explanation: Two-sided network effects occur when the value of a platform increases for one user group as the adoption rate of a complementary user group grows.
